name: paper_sige_hbt_resfb
description: Wideband SiGe-HBT cascode LNA with resistive-plus-capacitive feedback and shunt peaking. Q1 common-emitter input stage, Q2 common-base cascode stage; a series feedback resistor RF in parallel with a feedback capacitor CF runs from the collector tank back to Q1's base; inductive emitter degeneration (LE) sets the real part of the input match; a series base inductor (LB) and input DC-block cap (Cin) form the input network; the load/peaking inductor LC together with a shunt-peaking damping resistor RSP flattens the gain to the band edge; an output DC-block cap (Cout) drives the 50-ohm load. Cited paper transcription -- topology + published Table-1 values transcribed, no value invented.
source_family: Wideband SiGe-HBT common-emitter/common-base cascode LNA with resistive-capacitive shunt feedback and inductive shunt peaking

cited_paper.title: Wideband SiGe-HBT LNA with Resistive Feedback and Shunt Peaking

The topology description (Q1 common-emitter, Q2 common-base cascode; resistor+capacitor negative feedback loop from Q2 collector to Q1 base; inductive emitter degeneration LE) and the full component table (Table 1) were read directly from the text.

device_map: Cin (VIN1 B1) capacitor  -- input DC block, 2 x 3.1 pF
LB (B1 G1) inductor      -- series base inductor, 150 pH
Q1 (CASC G1 E1) npn      -- common-emitter input; C=cascode node CASC, B=G1, E=E1
LE (E1 VSS) inductor     -- inductive emitter degeneration, 20 pH
Q2 (CTANK VDD CASC) npn  -- common-base cascode; C=tank CTANK, B=VDD(AC gnd), E=CASC
LC (CTANK VDD) inductor  -- load / shunt-peaking inductor, 900 pH
RSP (CTANK VDD) resistor -- shunt-peaking damping resistor, 69 ohm
RF (CTANK G1) resistor   -- feedback resistor, 240 ohm
CF (CTANK G1) capacitor  -- feedback capacitor, 360 fF
Cout (CTANK VOUT1) capacitor -- output DC block, 2.2 pF
approximations_and_ambiguities: APPROXIMATION: RSP is modelled as a resistor in parallel with LC between CTANK and VDD (a parallel shunt-peaking damping network). The paper labels RSP a 'shunt peaking resistor'; whether it sits in series with LC or in parallel with it is not stated unambiguously in the fetched text. Parallel damping is the more common shunt-peaking realisation and is used here; flagged rather than guessed silently.

APPROXIMATION: Cin's '2 x 3.1 pF' (two capacitors, likely a differential/balanced input pair) is transcribed as a single lumped input DC-block cap Cin, because AnalogGenie is topology-only and the single-ended core is the family instance being represented.

The Q1/Q2 base bias network (the DC path that sets the operating point of the common-emitter and common-base bases) is not drawn as separate bias devices; Q2's base is tied to VDD as the AC ground of a cascode, which is the canonical single-ended cascode representation. No bias resistor values were invented.

transcription_confidence: HIGH for the family and the core cascode + resistive-capacitive-feedback + shunt-peaking topology (read directly from the paper text and Table 1) and for all Table-1 magnitudes (transcribed verbatim). MEDIUM only for the series-vs-parallel placement of RSP relative to LC (see approximations).
excluded_paper_check: Independent of, and unrelated to, the Kanchetla et al. TMTT 2022 paper this pipeline is blind-reproducing. This is a wideband SiGe-HBT feedback LNA (broadband, resistive-feedback family); it does not derive from and nor references the excluded GNSS narrowband CMOS design. The fetched article contains no mention of Kanchetla, NavIC, or BeiDou.
